output.methodChoice: Kepner-Tregoe specification (IS/IS NOT by press, supplier, shift), then ACH across the four hypotheses, plus a provenance check of the manager's and technician's accounts.
output.brief:
The rejects come from an interaction. Arnholt resin arrives wetter than Quillan, about 0.27–0.33% water against 0.11–0.14%. Dryer D7 handles it, with an outlet reading of 0.07%. Dryer D5 has degraded: its dew point is −16 to −19 instead of −40, and its alarm limit was loosened in week 31. D5 can't dry Arnholt below the 0.20% limit, so wet resin reaches Press 5. Press 5 with Arnholt rejects about 10% of parts. Press 5 with Quillan runs at 0.9%, and Press 7 with either resin runs at about 0.7–0.8%. One lot dried in a clean portable dryer gave 0.8% rejects on Press 5, against 10.4% through D5.

The new operators are not the cause. Their reject rates match the experienced operators' on both resins. Second shift looks worse only because all of its VX runs on Press 5, which now takes the Arnholt lots. Do not put the six on improvement plans, and do not drop Arnholt entirely.

This week:
1. Repair D5 and confirm its dew point is back at −40.
2. Restore the original alarm limit.
3. Keep Arnholt off D5 until that is verified.
4. Check moisture at the press throat for every resin lot.

The cause of the wetter Arnholt resin is still open. The north annex storage is a plausible reason but is not tested, so don't pay to move the resin yet. Confidence is high.
